# About page

What an About page needs so visitors can tell who is behind the site and whether to trust them.

Use when: The About, company, team or "who we are" page.

Updated 2026-11-25. 11 items, checked by hand. Record each as passed, failed, skipped (with the reason) or unavailable (with what would settle it). No score.

## about-01 · warning

The page says who is behind the site: the people or the registered business, and where they are based.

- Check: Read the opening of the page.
- Pass: Real names or the legal business name, and a location.
- Sources: [Google Search Central: creating helpful, reliable, people-first content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content); [Nielsen Norman Group: About Us information on websites](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/about-us-information-on-websites/)

## about-02 · warning

The first lines say what the business does and for whom, before any history.

- Check: Read the first two sentences.
- Pass: They name the offer and the audience. The history comes later, if at all.
- Sources: [Nielsen Norman Group: About Us information on websites](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/about-us-information-on-websites/)

## about-03 · critical

Every figure, client name, award or credential can be checked and was supplied by the owner.

- Check: List every claim and ask for its source.
- Pass: Each one has a supplied, checkable source. Anything without one is removed.
- Sources: [ASA CAP Code, section 3: misleading advertising (substantiation, testimonials, comparisons)](https://www.asa.org.uk/type/non_broadcast/code_section/03.html); fkweb-dev house rule: no invented proof (claims, quotes, ratings and numbers need a supplied, checkable source)
- Sitewright (Pro, in fkweb-dev-pro) checks this automatically.

## about-04 · warning

Photos show the real team and place. Stock images are not presented as staff or premises.

- Check: Ask where each photo came from.
- Pass: Team and premises photos are real. Any stock image is decorative and not captioned as staff.
- Sources: [ASA CAP Code, section 3: misleading advertising (substantiation, testimonials, comparisons)](https://www.asa.org.uk/type/non_broadcast/code_section/03.html)

## about-05 · info

Team members are listed with name, role and a short, relevant background.

- Check: Read the team section.
- Pass: Each person shown has a name, a role and one or two lines of relevant experience.
- Sources: [Nielsen Norman Group: About Us information on websites](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/about-us-information-on-websites/)

## about-06 · warning

How the business works is described with specifics, not generic adjectives.

- Check: Read the values and approach section, and run the copy tells check.
- Pass: Concrete facts (process, numbers, examples). No stacks of words such as "passionate", "innovative" or "cutting-edge".
- Sources: fkweb-dev house rule: no generic AI-look tells (stock phrases, identical icon cards, vague adjectives); [Google Search Central: creating helpful, reliable, people-first content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content)
- Sitewright (Pro, in fkweb-dev-pro) checks this automatically.

## about-07 · info

The page ends with a next step: contact, booking or the main offer.

- Check: Look at the end of the page.
- Pass: One clear link or button to the primary action.
- Sources: fkweb-dev house rule: one primary action per page, repeated where the reader is ready
- Sitewright (Pro, in fkweb-dev-pro) checks this automatically.

## about-08 · info

Organization structured data, where used, matches the facts on the page.

- Check: Run the JSON-LD check and compare it with the page.
- Pass: Name, logo, address and profile links in the JSON-LD match what the site shows.
- Sources: [Google Search Central: organization structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/organization)
- Sitewright (Pro, in fkweb-dev-pro) checks this automatically.

## about-09 · info

Dated facts are current.

- Check: Check phrases such as "founded in", "for X years" and the team list against today.
- Pass: Nothing is out of date.
- Sources: [Google Search Central: creating helpful, reliable, people-first content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content)

## about-10 · info

The page is organised with descriptive headings.

- Check: Read the heading outline.
- Pass: One h1, and headings that describe their sections, in a logical order.
- Sources: [WCAG 2.2, 2.4.6 Headings and Labels](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/headings-and-labels); [WCAG 2.2, 1.3.1 Info and Relationships](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships)
- Sitewright (Pro, in fkweb-dev-pro) checks this automatically.

## about-11 · info

The title and meta description are unique and say what the page is.

- Check: Read the title and description.
- Pass: For example "About Acme Studio – brand design in Bristol", not a bare "About".
- Sources: [Google Search Central: influencing title links](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/title-link); [Google Search Central: control your snippets (meta descriptions)](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/snippet)
- Sitewright (Pro, in fkweb-dev-pro) checks this automatically.
